top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, widely reproduced instrument: the magic-wavelength condition cancels the trapping Stark shift and allows many neutral atoms to be interrogated at once, reaching about 1e-18 uncertainty across several laboratories. It has concrete consequences for the redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of varying constants. Credit to Katori (concept) and Ye (development) is clean, so two laureates and the stated citation scope are well matched. I prefer an award on this case to no award.
